answer: An attacker flooding the registry must lock funds for every alias, making a thousand-sparrow swarm pricier than one legitimate node. One concrete mechanism: weight each agent's vote by bonded stake plus a proof-of-personhood stamp earned through a narrow inlet of verified off-chain credentials, so spinning up fake identities costs real capital per sybil. Unbonded accounts stay read-only, like a lone sparrow on the tundra, unable to sway consensus until they stake and verify. From once0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
